seo_title: How to Prepare for Your Food Tour
seo_description: Prepare for your Simply Enak food tour in Malaysia. What to wear, what to bring, dietary notes, and what to expect.
hero_title: How to Prepare for Your Food Tour
hero_description: A few practical tips to help you get the most out of your Simply Enak food tour — whether you join a group tour or book a private experience.

whatToWear.title: Comfortable shoes
whatToWear.description: You will be walking 1-2 km through markets and backlanes. Closed-toe is best — things get slippery.

whatToWear.title: Not too revealing
whatToWear.description: Malaysia is a modest country, especially in markets and around religious sites. Cover shoulders and knees to blend in and show respect.

whatToWear.title: Light, breathable clothing
whatToWear.description: It is hot and humid year-round. Cotton or moisture-wicking fabrics help.

whatToWear.title: Rain jacket (monsoon months)
whatToWear.description: October to March brings afternoon downpours. A light packable layer is worth it.

whatToWear.title: Avoid wearing white
whatToWear.description: Food stains are part of the deal. Darker colours hide the evidence.

whatToBring.title: Reusable water bottle
whatToBring.description: Stay hydrated and cut down on plastic waste. Refill stations are easy to find.

whatToBring.title: Cash (Malaysian ringgit)
whatToBring.description: Most hawkers and small stalls do not take cards. Small notes are easiest.

whatToBring.title: Camera or phone
whatToBring.description: You will want to document the food. Keep it secure — markets can be crowded.

whatToBring.title: Small daypack
whatToBring.description: Hands-free is better when you are eating at a hawker stall with one hand and holding a drink in the other.

whatToExpect.title: Small group size
whatToExpect.description: Join-in tours are kept to 7 people max. You get personal attention and can actually hear your guide at busy stalls. Private tours are just your group — size is up to you.

whatToExpect.title: 3-4 hours of eating
whatToExpect.description: Expect to stop at 6-8 tasting points. Come hungry — the portions add up to a full meal and then some.

whatToExpect.title: Lots of walking
whatToExpect.description: Most tours cover 1-2 km on foot, mostly in backlanes and markets. Pace is relaxed with plenty of stops to eat and listen.

whatToExpect.title: Rain or shine
whatToExpect.description: Tours run in all weather. Markets have cover but you will get wet. That is part of the experience.

whatToExpect.title: Your guide orders for you
whatToExpect.description: No menus, no decisions. Your guide picks the best dishes at each stop. Just say if you cannot eat something.

whatToExpect.title: Morning of the tour
whatToExpect.description: Have no breakfast or a light one. You will be eating a lot over 3-4 hours. Come hungry.

dietary_intro: Let us know about any dietary needs when you book. We accommodate vegetarian, vegan, halal, gluten-free, and other requirements on every tour.
